text:
elaine: heads-up — multiple customers seeing 503s (hosted) starting ~08:12 PDT. Primary pattern: auth-heavy bursts → upstream inference worker crashes / container restarts. acme-analytics reported 30% request failure rate.

sanjay: are these tied to a specific model or large-context requests? any logs yet?

elaine: early look shows auth tokens valid; gateway returns 502/503 then upstream logs show GPU OOM or SIGSEGV in runtime. sample trace from worker-7: 
```
[2025-04-07T15:12:41Z] runtime ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2025-04-07T15:12:41Z] infer-worker[pid=4201] SIGSEGV at 0x7f8...
[stack] at attention_kernel.cu:142
container restart triggered by liveness probe
```

maria: I see a concurrent spike in authenticated requests (auth service showed 3x p95). Could be a burst that pushes batching to larger sizes, increasing GPU mem.

devon: rolling back dynbatch config from last deploy would be quick to test — that change increased max_batch_size from 8 -> 32 yesterday. If we force smaller batch sizes it might avoid OOMs.

elaine: can we also enable fallback routing to dedicated capacity for affected customers while we triage? acme asked for an emergency SLA call.

sanjay: ops-bot, route-check for acme-analytics: any dedicated capacity available in us-west?

ops-bot: @sanjay checking pools... matched pool: redwood-dedicated-usw-1 has 5 idle GPUs. Routing policy update available: /routing promote acme-analytics -> dedicated-usw. Confirm to apply.

sanjay: apply it.

ops-bot: routing change applied. traffic for acme-analytics shifted to dedicated-usw-1.

maria: acme reports immediate improvement (timeouts drop). They still see some 500s from older requests in flight.

devon: for root cause: capture full heap snapshot and nvml metrics for worker-7 prior to next crash. Also capture host dmesg. Adding repro steps: reproduce with auth-heavy burst + make toolcall with large context (~16k tokens) to model gpt-open-16k-quant.

elaine: backup mitigation: temporarily cap tenant batch_size to 8 and limit concurrent sessions to 50 for hosted customers that show the spike. I'll coordinate with support to notify customers.

sanjay: quick patch plan: revert batch_size max, add guard rails in runtime to reject single requests that would require >12GB on GPU (fail fast), and add a watchdog that drains heavy requests instead of letting OOM happen.

maria: I've started a narrow canary: reduce max_batch for pool upstream-1 and monitoring p95 GPU mem. Sending dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/pools/upstream-1 (shared).

elaine: support update -> "We have routed your traffic to dedicated capacity and are implementing safeguards. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." :thumbsup:

devon: note for postmortem: include exact config commit (gitsha: 9f3b2a1), recent optimizer kernel roll (nvfuser v2.1), and model quant swap that went out 12h ago. Suspect interaction between quantized kernels + dynbatch expansion.

sanjay: assigning oncall:devon for immediate triage and oncall:infra for kernel-level debug.

devon: ok I'm grabbing the heap dumps now. If anyone sees a repeat, add logs to /var/log/infer/worker-7/crash-*.tgz and ping here.

elaine: thanks everyone. I'll keep CS posted and set up a 11:00 standup if we need a cross-team bridge.

maria: one more: add a short-term rate limit on auth tokens per-tenant to smooth the burst. We can relax after root cause.

devon: agreed. Implemented soft-rate-limit for tenants with spike > 2x baseline (config id: rl-2025-041).

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2025-2047, priority P1.

elaine: closing loop for now — routing helped immediate customer impact. still tracking root cause and will postpostmortem.
